facts.note: As of Oct 2026, Anthropic is the most valuable private AI lab: its May 2026 Series H valued it at $965B post-money, above OpenAI's $852B. Bloomberg called this the first time Anthropic's valuation exceeded OpenAI's.
The two leaders are roughly tied on revenue run-rate: Anthropic passed $65B by end of July 2026 (Reuters), and OpenAI was reported near $70B by late September 2026 (Axios).
SpaceX, which absorbed xAI in Feb 2026, listed on Nasdaq as SPCX on June 12, 2026, raising $75B at $135 per share, the largest IPO on record per coverage. It then agreed to buy Cursor for $60B.
Anthropic is now targeting an IPO as soon as mid-November 2026, with marketing possibly starting the week of Nov 9. Altman has said OpenAI will not list in 2026.

Amazon booked $53.4B of mostly Anthropic-related non-operating gains in Q2 2026 while shutting its AGI SF Lab and moving most Nova models to maintenance mode. It is betting on hosting frontier labs over building its own frontier model.

Frontier labs are now buying compute from each other: Anthropic's Series H announcement lists GPU capacity from SpaceX's Colossus 1 and 2, alongside 5GW from Amazon and 5GW of TPUs from Google and Broadcom.
Nvidia became the neolab kingmaker and exit route in 2026: investments in Thinking Machines (Mar) and SSI (Jul), a $6B Poolside license deal (Aug), and FT-reported talks to buy Reflection (Oct).

Capital-markets wave: Zhipu (2513) and MiniMax (00100) listed in Hong Kong in Jan 2026; StepFun, Moonshot and 01.AI are preparing HK IPOs and DeepSeek is prepping a Shanghai STAR listing. Zhipu/MiniMax six-month lock-ups (~US$11.5B of shares) expired around July 2026.

BIS rule effective 2026-01-15 moved US exports of H200/MI325X-class chips to China from presumption of denial to case-by-case review, with conditions (third-party testing, KYC, China volume capped at 50% of US-shipped compute) alongside a 25% US cut/duty arrangement.
AMD agreed to acquire World Labs in an all-stock deal worth about $8.2B; Fei-Fei Li to become AMD EVP and chief scientist, closing expected by end-2026.
SpaceX closed its $60B all-stock purchase of Cursor on 2026-08-14, the largest VC-backed startup acquisition on record, folding it into SpaceXAI.

Price compression: average inference price fell ~43% in ten weeks, from ~$2.04 to ~$1.16-1.18 per million tokens (late May to early Aug 2026), after OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing 80%; ARK measured $2.07 to $1.02.
Nvidia's data-center revenue hit $89.0B in its quarter ended July 26, 2026 (+117% YoY), and it guided total revenue to $108B for the next quarter while assuming zero China data-center compute sales.
AI-credit stress hit in mid-October: CoreWeave's 5-yr CDS topped 1,000 bps with bonds yielding >15% (2032s ~77 cents), and Oracle CDS widened to a record ~288 bps.
Waymo reported 500K+ paid rides per week, 4,000+ vehicles and 14 US cities as of Sept 1, 2026, targeting 1M weekly trips by end of 2026 (up from 400K+/week across 6 metros in Feb).
Character.AI filed Chapter 11 on 2026-10-12 after compute costs ($56.1M Jan-Aug 2026) dwarfed revenue (peak ~$5.3M/month) amid teen-harm suits; Disney bid $20M for an IP license and hired most staff.

layers.name: Model labs
layers.what: Companies that train foundation models: frontier labs, neolabs, open-weight, China, media and world models.

cats.title: The frontier race
cats.overview: Five organizations train the largest general-purpose models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI (now part of SpaceX) and Meta. Two of them, Anthropic and OpenAI, are private companies valued above $850B each, are roughly tied on revenue run-rate, and are both preparing to go public.
happening: Anthropic's $65B Series H in May valued it at $965B post-money, above OpenAI's $852B from its $122B round in March.
Run-rate revenue: Anthropic passed $65B by end of July; OpenAI was reported near $70B in late September (anonymous sources via Axios).
Anthropic is targeting an IPO as soon as mid-November. OpenAI filed confidentially in June but Altman says it won't list in 2026.
xAI was absorbed by SpaceX in February. SpaceX listed on Nasdaq (SPCX) in June and then agreed to buy Cursor for $60B.
Leadership churn hit the incumbents: Demis Hassabis stepped back at Google DeepMind (Aug 5) and OpenAI lost about 14 senior executives this year.

cats.title: Big Tech's model bets
cats.overview: The other giants split into builders and hosts. Microsoft trains its own MAI models while staying a major OpenAI shareholder. Amazon scaled back its own models to focus on hosting labs like Anthropic. Apple rebuilt Siri on Google's Gemini. Nvidia sells the chips, publishes open models and invests across the labs.
happening: The April 2026 Microsoft–OpenAI amendment made Microsoft's license non-exclusive through 2032 and let OpenAI sell on any cloud.
AI capex keeps rising: Alphabet guides $195–205B for 2026, Meta $130–145B, and Microsoft spent about $41B in its June quarter alone.
Amazon booked $53.4B of mostly Anthropic-related gains in Q2 while closing its AGI SF Lab and moving most Nova models to maintenance mode.
John Ternus became Apple's CEO on Sep 1, and the Gemini-built Siri shipped with iOS 27 on Sep 14.

cats.title: The neolab wave
cats.overview: Neolabs are new research labs built around famous researchers. Many raise $300M to $2B as a first round, at multi-billion valuations, before shipping a product. TechCrunch nicknamed these giant first rounds “coconut rounds.”
happening: 2026 mega-seeds: AMI Labs (Yann LeCun) $1.03B; Ineffable Intelligence (David Silver) $1.1B at $5.1B; Humans& $480M at $4.48B.
Thinking Machines (Mira Murati) shipped its first open model, Inkling, in July and grew to about 200 people, but three co-founders left for OpenAI in January.
Nvidia became the neolabs' kingmaker and exit route: investments in Thinking Machines and SSI, a $6B license deal with Poolside, and reported talks to buy Reflection.
Investor appetite is cooling. Poolside could not raise $2B in time for its planned GPU cluster.

notes.note: Radical Ventures counts 40+ independent neolabs that have raised ~$40B; 13 North American/European model providers closed $1B+ rounds since start of 2025, 8 of them neolabs, and DeepMind alumni account for 40+ neolab founders.
Per an FT account cited in a Sept 2026 summary, neolabs raised about $24B in the two most recent quarters, nearly 5x what OpenAI and Anthropic raised combined before ChatGPT.

NEA estimates AI research labs carry ~$1.68T aggregate private valuation (PitchBook, Apr 30 2026), with frontier generalists (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, SSI) taking 93.6%, leaving ~6% for all other neolab segments.
Seed sizes are extreme: Ricursive hit a $4B valuation two months after launch, Flapping Airplanes raised a $180M seed, and Dealroom data shows $18.8B invested in AI startups founded since 2025.

cats.title: Open-weight & enterprise model makers
cats.overview: A second tier sells models that businesses and governments can run themselves: open weights, private deployment and “sovereign” hosting. Much of the mid-stage model work lives here, and so does most of the consolidation.
happening: Mistral raised a €3B Series D at more than €21B in September, the largest equity round ever for a European tech company.
Cohere signed a merger with Aleph Alpha on Sep 16. AI21 cut 110 of 180 staff in May and stopped building its own models.
Reflection AI closed a round at $25B pre-money in April, and the FT reported in October that Nvidia is in talks to buy it or deepen its stake.
Small, fast-growing labs: Prime Intellect raised a $130M Series A at $1B and says it has passed $100M annualized revenue; Nous Research raised a $90M Series B (reported $1.5B).

cats.title: China's labs
cats.overview: China runs a parallel frontier. Its models are mostly open-weight and far cheaper, and are increasingly trained on domestic chips because US exports of H200-class GPUs are reviewed case by case and very few have shipped. Its labs are now going public in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
happening: Zhipu (2513.HK) listed Jan 8, the first public pure-play LLM company. Its H1 2026 revenue was about $142M, up about 400%.
MiniMax (00100.HK) listed Jan 9. DeepSeek took its first outside money in June (about $7.4B at more than $50B) and has hired CITIC Securities for a possible Shanghai IPO.
A larger DeepSeek round (at least 80B yuan, about $12B) was reported near closing on Oct 6. It is not confirmed.
Moonshot (Kimi) told investors its annualized revenue passed $1B in August, after a raise at about $35B.

cats.title: Sovereign & international labs
cats.overview: Governments are paying for “sovereign AI”: domestic labs so their country doesn't depend on US or Chinese models. The money comes from national funds, state investors and large local companies.
happening: Japan's Sakana AI raised a $135M Series B at about $2.6B and added Mitsubishi Electric as an investor in March.
India's Sarvam AI raised $234M (first close of a $300M Series B) at about $1.5B in June, led by HCLTech. Krutrim has struggled, with layoffs.
Korea's national fund put about KRW 560B (about $380M) into Upstage in May. LG released K-EXAONE 2.0 under Apache 2.0 in July.
In the Gulf, G42 (UAE) builds Stargate UAE with OpenAI and Oracle, and Saudi Arabia's PIF-owned Humain is raising a $2.5B data-center fund.

cats.title: Generative media
cats.overview: Image, video, voice and music models are a separate race with their own leaders. The surprise of 2026 is that some app-layer companies built on other people's models now earn more than many model labs.
happening: ElevenLabs reached about $500M ARR (April) and ran a $300M employee tender at $22B (September).
Higgsfield, largely built on third-party models, hit a $700M run-rate and raised $400M at $5.4B in August. HeyGen passed $200M ARR on about $74M raised.
OpenAI said in March it would shut down Sora in both the app and the API.
Music lawsuits are splitting: Warner settled with Suno while UMG and Sony keep suing it. UMG and Warner settled with Udio.

cats.title: World models
cats.overview: World models generate interactive, explorable environments instead of text or fixed clips. They are pitched for games, simulation and training robots, and in 2026 they became acquisition targets.
happening: AMD agreed on Sep 28 to buy Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for about $8.2B in stock, closing by end of 2026.
Decart raised $300M at about $4B in May. Anthropic reportedly walked away from buying it for about $6B in September, after Decart had turned down a higher Nvidia offer.
Odyssey raised a $310M Series B at $1.45B, and General Intuition raised $320M at $2.3B (lead investor reported differently by different outlets).
Yann LeCun's AMI Labs is also a world-model lab. It is filed under neolabs.

cats.title: AI for science & biology
cats.overview: Labs that train models on biology, chemistry and materials instead of internet text, aiming to discover drugs and new materials. Money is concentrating in a few model-first labs, while public markets give their IPOs a lukewarm reception.
happening: Isomorphic Labs (Alphabet-backed) raised a $2.1B Series B in May. Chai Discovery went from $1.3B to $3.8B, and Lila Sciences was reported in talks at about $8.5B.
Lukewarm IPOs: Generate Biomedicines fell 21% on its first day (February), while Insilico rose about 25% on its Hong Kong debut.
Clinical milestones: Insilico's AI-discovered rentosertib completed Phase 2a. Recursion's Q2 revenue fell to $7.7M and it is cutting costs.
Materials discovery is heating up: CuspAI raised $450M at about $2.6B, alongside Periodic Labs.

notes.note: Isomorphic Labs' $2.1B Series B (May 2026) and Earendil Labs' $787M combined financings dominate a 2026 tracker of ~22 AI drug-discovery rounds of $10M+; most other rounds are $10-80M seeds and Series As.

Chai Discovery went from $1.3B (Dec 2025) to $3.8B (Jul 2026) valuation, and Lila Sciences was reported in talks at ~$8.5B pre-money in June 2026, showing capital concentrating in a few model-first bio labs.
Public exits are lukewarm: Generate Biomedicines' $400M Nasdaq IPO (Feb 2026) closed down 21% on day one, while Insilico's Dec 2025 HK IPO (~$293M) rose ~25% on debut.
Clinical milestones: Insilico's AI-discovered rentosertib completed Phase 2a in IPF, and MindRank's AI-derived oral GLP-1 MDR-001 is in Phase III in China.
Recursion's Q2 2026 revenue fell to $7.7M from $19.2M as partnership revenue dipped, and it cut 2026 opex guidance to under $375M with runway into early 2028.
Materials discovery is heating up: CuspAI raised a $450M Series B at ~$2.6B (5x its Sept 2025 valuation) in July 2026, alongside covered Periodic Labs.

layers.intro: Companies that train foundation models: the frontier labs, new research labs, open-weight and enterprise model makers, China's labs, sovereign labs, generative media, world models, and science labs.

layers.name: Chips, compute & clouds
layers.what: The silicon and the data centers: GPUs and custom chips, hyperscalers, neoclouds, power.

cats.title: Chips & custom silicon
cats.overview: Every AI model runs on a few kinds of chips. Nvidia's GPUs dominate. The big buyers increasingly design their own chips with partners like Broadcom and Marvell, all of it is made at TSMC, and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has become the tightest bottleneck.
happening: Nvidia's quarter ended July 26 brought $96.2B of revenue, $89.0B of it from data centers (+117%). It guided $108B for the next quarter, assuming no China data-center sales.
Broadcom's AI chip revenue was $16.7B for the quarter (+221%). OpenAI (“Jalapeño”), Meta (MTIA) and Microsoft (Maia) all ship their own chips, and Anthropic is hiring a chip team.
Google now rents TPUs to outside customers: Meta signed a deal, and Anthropic has up to 1M chips (about 5GW).
Memory is the binding constraint. SK Hynix's CEO calls 2027 the worst supply year on record, and SK Hynix raised $26.5B in a US listing.
AMD signed equity-linked chip deals with OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic and is buying Taalas.

notes.note: Nvidia's data-center revenue hit $89.0B in its quarter ended July 26, 2026 (+117% YoY), and it guided total revenue to $108B for the next quarter while assuming zero China data-center compute sales.

Custom silicon is scaling fast: Broadcom's AI chip revenue reached $16.7B in its August quarter (+221% YoY) with $21.7B guided next, while OpenAI (Jalapeno), Meta (MTIA), Microsoft (Maia) and now Anthropic (hiring a chip team) all design their own accelerators.

Google now rents and sells TPUs outside its own walls: Meta signed a multibillion-dollar TPU deal, Anthropic has up to 1M Ironwood chips / 5GW over five years, and Google reportedly aims to capture up to 10% of Nvidia's data-center revenue.
Memory is the binding constraint: SK Hynix's CEO calls 2027 the worst supply year in industry history with shortages lasting to 2030.
Export controls loosened but stayed messy: the US allowed H200 sales to vetted Chinese buyers with a 25% cut to Washington, while Beijing restricted purchases.

cats.title: AI chip startups
cats.overview: Dozens of startups are building chips to run AI more cheaply than GPUs, especially for inference. In 2026 public markets reopened for them, valuations jumped, and the usual exit became a license-and-hire deal or a tuck-in acquisition.
happening: Cerebras listed in May at $185 a share, raising $5.55B in the year's largest US IPO. An aggregator now puts its market cap at about $29B.
Nvidia took a reported ~$20B non-exclusive license from Groq and hired its founders, while Groq carries on as an inference cloud. Marvell bought Celestial AI, and AMD is buying Taalas.
Valuations jumped: Etched went from $5B to $21B within months, Positron from $1B to $5B, and SambaNova raised at $11B after nearly selling to Intel for about $1.6B.
Chip startups raised about $8.4B in Q1, $6B+ in Q2 and $8.5B+ in Q3 2026.

notes.note: Chip-startup funding stayed hot all year: roughly 80 semiconductor startups raised $8.4B in Q1 2026, over $6B in Q2 and over $8.5B in Q3, with about $7.5B of Q3 going to 22 rounds of $100M+.

Exits favour licensing and tuck-ins over classic buyouts: Nvidia's reported ~$20B non-exclusive license plus hire of Groq's founders (Dec 2025), Marvell's completed Celestial AI deal (Feb 2026), and AMD's announced deal to buy Taalas (Aug 2026).
Public markets reopened for AI chips: Cerebras priced its IPO at $185 on May 14, 2026, raising $5.55B and opening 89% higher in the largest US IPO of the year.

Late-stage valuations jumped within months: Etched went from $5B (Dec 2025) to $10.3B (July) to $21B (August 2026), Positron from $1B to $5B, and SambaNova raised at $11B after nearly selling to Intel for ~$1.6B.

Incumbents are shopping: Tenstorrent held takeover talks with Intel and Qualcomm in May 2026, and Nvidia is pulling startups into its orbit via NVLink Fusion partnerships (d-Matrix, Ayar Labs) and equity stakes.

cats.title: Clouds & neoclouds
cats.overview: AI models are trained and served in rented data centers. The big three clouds and Oracle sell most of that capacity. GPU-focused “neoclouds” (CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe, Lambda, Nscale) grew fast on borrowed money, and by October markets were testing how much debt they can carry.
happening: Q2 cloud growth sped up: AWS +37% to $42.2B, Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% to $24.8B. Microsoft's contracted backlog is $678B and Google Cloud's $514B.
2026 capex guides were raised again: Amazon about $220B, Alphabet $195–205B, and Microsoft $255–260B for its next fiscal year.
Oracle's backlog reached $664B, but quarterly free cash flow was about −$5B and it sold $20B of stock.

Credit stress in mid-October: CoreWeave's stock fell about 25% in a week and its credit-default swaps hit a record near 1,195 bps, with bonds yielding about 15%. Oracle's swaps hit a record. Nscale's IPO faces pressure to price lower, and Firmus cancelled its IPO.
Crusoe raised $3.9B at $30.9B (September). Lambda is not public yet and is targeting a 2027 IPO.

notes.note: Q2 2026 cloud growth re-accelerated across the big three: AWS +37% to $42.2B, Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% to $24.8B; Microsoft commercial RPO reached $678B and Google Cloud backlog $514B.
2026 capex guides were raised again in July: Amazon to ~$220B (from ~$200B) and Alphabet to $195-205B (from $180-190B); Microsoft guided FY2027 capex to $255-260B.
Oracle's AI build is stretching its balance sheet: Q1 FY27 RPO $664B but free cash flow about -$5B, funded partly by a $20B at-the-market stock sale.
AI-credit stress hit in mid-October: CoreWeave's 5-yr CDS topped 1,000 bps with bonds yielding >15% (2032s ~77 cents), and Oracle CDS widened to a record ~288 bps.

The neocloud IPO window is wobbling: Nscale (filed seeking up to $35B) faces investor pressure toward $16-19B, Firmus cancelled its Australian IPO, and CoreWeave yields reached ~15% vs a 9.67% issue rate.

cats.title: Data centers, power & networking
cats.overview: The physical layer: buildings, electricity, cooling and the networking that links chips together. Power is now the main thing that slows AI growth, and huge infrastructure funds are paying record prices.
happening: GE Vernova's gas-turbine backlog plus reservations reached 116 GW. Grid delays cost an Nscale UK site its Microsoft anchor tenant, and OpenAI dropped Stargate UK over energy costs.
Stargate had about 0.3 GW running in April against more than 9 GW planned, mostly due by late 2028.
AIP, MGX and BlackRock's GIP bought Aligned Data Centers for $40B (July).
Nuclear startups raised a record $6B+ in 2026, but newly listed ones trade far below their highs. Fervo raised $1.89B in its IPO, and Helion raised at $15.5B.
Networking startups raised big: Nexthop AI $500M at $4.2B, Upscale AI $190M at $2B.

notes.note: Power equipment is a bottleneck: GE Vernova's gas-turbine backlog plus slot reservations reached 116 GW in Q2 2026 (target >=125 GW by year-end), with data-center orders >$5B year to date.
Grid access is delaying sites: Nscale's Loughton (UK) project lost Microsoft as anchor tenant after grid power slipped to the 2030s, and OpenAI dropped Stargate UK citing energy costs.
Infrastructure and sovereign capital is paying record prices: AIP, MGX and BlackRock's GIP closed a $40B acquisition of Aligned Data Centers (6.4 GW+) and committed $5B more for expansion.
Stargate had only ~0.3 GW operational in April 2026 against >9 GW planned across seven US sites, most due for completion in Q4 2028.

Nuclear startups raised a record >$6B in 2026 (per Crunchbase), but newly listed names (X-energy, Deep Fission, Standard Nuclear) trade far below highs and Oklo is down nearly two-thirds from its peak.

layers.intro: The physical foundation: chips, memory, clouds, data centers, power and networking. Most companies here are public, so cards show market cap and the latest quarter instead of a funding round.

layers.name: Dev tools & infra
layers.what: Software that builders use to make AI products: coding agents, inference, data, evals, agent frameworks.

cats.title: Coding agents & AI IDEs
cats.overview: Coding is AI's first giant market. Two startups led it: Cursor, now owned by SpaceX, and Cognition (Devin and Windsurf). The model labs sell competing tools directly (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI), and most other independents are being acquired or squeezed.
happening: SpaceX closed its $60B all-stock purchase of Cursor on Aug 14. Cursor's run-rate had passed $2B in February.
Cognition raised more than $2B at $48B in September, up from $26B in May, and says its run-rate crossed $1B.
Factory went from a $1.5B to a $5B valuation in five months. Harness bought Augment Code's core products and team (Oct 8), and Anaconda bought Kilo Code (July).
Margins are thin. Cursor ran at negative gross margin until recently, and in April GitHub paused Copilot Pro signups while Codex moved to token pricing.

notes.note: SpaceX closed its $60B all-stock purchase of Cursor on 2026-08-14, the largest VC-backed startup acquisition on record, folding it into SpaceXAI.
Cursor ran at negative gross margins until recently and still loses money on individual developers; only its own Composer model and cheaper models brought it slightly positive.
In April 2026 the labs and GitHub tightened coding-tool pricing: Copilot paused Pro signups and cut model access, Codex moved to token pricing, Gemini CLI's free tier lost Pro (blog source).
Consolidation is accelerating: Anaconda bought Kilo Code (Jul 2026), Harness bought Augment Code's core assets (Oct 2026), and Cognition acquired TierZero, The Interaction Company and Dioxus.
Capital is concentrating in a few winners: Cognition raised >$2B at $48B in Sep 2026, up from $26B in May, and Factory went from $1.5B to $5B in five months.
JetBrains reported its own AI development costs rose about tenfold in six months, a sign of token-cost pressure even for incumbents.

cats.title: App builders
cats.overview: App builders let non-engineers make working apps from a prompt. Revenue grew faster here than almost anywhere in software, but profit margins depend on how much the builder pays for model calls.
happening: Lovable raised $400M at $13.3B in August and is on track for about a $600M run-rate.
Replit raised $400M at $9B in March, ran at about $525M in April, and targets $1B ARR by year-end.
Emergent went from a $300M to a $1.5B valuation between January and July. Vercel, home of v0, reported about $340M ARR in February.
Base44 (owned by Wix) had near-zero gross margin entering 2026 and expects about 60% in the second half after launching its own model.

notes.note: Base44's gross margin was near zero entering 2026; Wix guided it to ~60% in H2 2026 after launching its own model, showing vibe-coding margins depend on owning inference.
Lovable doubled its valuation to $13.3B in eight months with a $400M Series C, and is on track for a ~$600M run rate.
Replit tripled its valuation to $9B in six months (Mar 2026) and targets $1B ARR by end-2026; its 2025 gross margin reportedly ranged from 36% to -14% (aggregator).
Late entrants still raise fast: India-built Emergent went from $300M (Jan) to a $1.5B valuation (Jul 2026), and Rork raised a $15M seed for mobile app building.
Big platforms are distribution partners: Lovable apps run inside ChatGPT and Claude, and Lovable (Sep 2026) and Bolt (May 2026) both signed Microsoft partnerships.

cats.title: Code review, testing & on-call
cats.overview: As agents write more code, checking it becomes the bottleneck. This layer covers review bots, test automation, faster CI, and “AI SRE” agents that investigate production incidents.
happening: CodeRabbit raised $143M at $1.5B in August and has more than 17,000 customers. Cursor bought Graphite in December 2025.
Anthropic added multi-agent Code Review to Claude Code in March, at about $15–25 per review. A sponsored industry blog counts 30+ AI review tools.
AI SRE is frothy: Resolve AI was valued at $1B on about $4M ARR at its February Series A.
Tusk, a YC test-generation startup, announced it is shutting down (June).

notes.note: Cursor bought Graphite in Dec 2025, reportedly for well above its $290M valuation, showing coding-agent platforms absorbing the review layer.

Anthropic launched a multi-agent Code Review for Claude Code (Teams/Enterprise) in Mar 2026, priced by tokens at about $15-25 per review, so a model lab now competes directly with standalone reviewers.

A sponsored industry blog counts 30+ AI code review tools and estimates AI code review startups raised over $1.2B from Jan 2024 to Dec 2025, with seat pricing from free to about $35 per user per month.

Capital is concentrating in the leader: CodeRabbit raised $143M at $1.5B in Aug 2026 with 17,000+ customers, while YipitData panel data shows Sourcegraph leading enterprise and about 10% of mid-market firms using more than one reviewer.
AI SRE is frothy: Resolve AI reached a $1B valuation on roughly $4M ARR, competing with Sequoia/Kleiner-backed Traversal, Cleric and incumbent incident.io's agentic Investigations.

cats.title: Agent infrastructure
cats.overview: The picks and shovels for AI agents: frameworks to build them, cloud browsers and sandboxes to run them, tool and login access, memory, and web search APIs built for machines instead of people.
happening: Agent web search produced two $2B companies in a month: Parallel ($100M Series B, April) and Exa ($250M Series C at $2.2B, May). Perplexity's $1-per-1,000 search API is pushing prices down.
Consolidation: Nebius agreed to buy Tavily (February), Arcade bought the Smithery MCP registry (August), and Twilio absorbed Stytch.
Sandboxes are becoming interchangeable: OpenAI's Agents SDK supports at least seven providers. Browser infrastructure has seven or more funded players.
2026 rounds: Arcade $60M Series A, Firecrawl $75M Series B, Mastra $22M Series A, Natural $30M Series A (payments for agents).

notes.note: Web search for agents produced two $2B+ companies within a month: Parallel ($100M Series B at $2B, Apr 2026) and Exa ($250M Series C at $2.2B, May 2026).
Consolidation is under way: Nebius bought Tavily (Feb 2026, reportedly ~$275M), Arcade bought Smithery (Aug 2026), Twilio absorbed Stytch (Oct 2025) and Elastic bought Jina AI (Oct 2025).
Browser infrastructure is crowded: at least seven funded players (Browserbase, TinyFish, Airtop, Kernel, Browser Use, Anchor, Strawberry) had raised by late 2025.
Agent sandboxes are commoditizing: the OpenAI Agents SDK supports at least seven interchangeable providers (Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, Runloop, Vercel).
Search API prices are compressing: Perplexity added Fast Search at $1 per 1,000 requests in Sep 2026, versus Exa's roughly $5 per 1,000 cited by Sacra in Jan 2026.

cats.title: Inference & model serving
cats.overview: Inference companies run open and custom models for developers on rented GPUs. It is one of the fastest-growing businesses in AI and one of the most price-competitive.
happening: Top valuations: Fireworks $17.5B (July), Modal $15.75B (Oct 14), Baseten $13B (June), Together $8.3B (July). Fireworks and Modal each report more than $1B run-rate.
Average token prices fell about 43% in ten weeks (May to August) after OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80%.
Buyers are consolidating the layer: Cloudflare–Replicate, Modular–BentoML, Nscale–Anyscale (about $1.65B, reported), Baseten–Blaxel, Nebius–Inferize.
The open-source serving engines became companies: Inferact (vLLM) raised a $150M seed at $800M and RadixArk (SGLang) $100M at $400M.

notes.note: In May 2026 investors said inference startups were growing from $100M+ revenue bases, yet Baseten, Fireworks and Modal all lease GPUs and sell similar products, so customers switch on price and margins are thin.

Price compression: average inference price fell ~43% in ten weeks, from ~$2.04 to ~$1.16-1.18 per million tokens (late May to early Aug 2026), after OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing 80%; ARK measured $2.07 to $1.02.
Valuations are crowded at the top: Fireworks $17.5B (Jul 2026), Modal $15.75B (Oct 2026), Baseten $13B (Jun 2026), Together $8.3B (Jul 2026). Fireworks and Modal each report >$1B run-rate.

Consolidation by clouds and chipmakers: Cloudflare-Replicate (Nov 2025), Modular-BentoML (Feb 2026), Nscale-Anyscale (~$1.65B, Jul 2026), d-Matrix-Wallaroo (Aug 2026), Baseten-Blaxel (Sep 2026), Nebius-Inferize (Oct 2026).

Open-source serving engines became venture companies: vLLM's creators launched Inferact ($150M seed, $800M valuation) and SGLang spun out as RadixArk (~$400M valuation), both from Ion Stoica's Berkeley lab. The engine layer is now capitalized, so startups should look elsewhere for an opening.

cats.title: Training, fine-tuning & ML platforms
cats.overview: Tools for adapting and training models: model hubs, experiment tracking and fine-tuning. The first generation of these companies was mostly bought. The new wave sells reinforcement-learning post-training as a service.
happening: Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $13B including retention (Sep 3), closing in the first half of 2027.
CoreWeave bought Weights & Biases and OpenPipe, Rubrik bought Predibase, and OpenAI bought neptune.ai.
Applied Compute was valued at $1.3B in April on about $12.8M ARR, with talks at about $3B reported in August.
Inference companies are moving into training: Fireworks made its Training API generally available in August, and Modal plans RL products.

notes.note: NVIDIA agreed in Sep 2026 to buy Hugging Face for ~$13B including a retention pool, almost 3x its 2023 $4.5B valuation; close expected H1 2027 pending regulators.

First-generation MLOps/fine-tuning tools were mostly absorbed: CoreWeave bought Weights & Biases (closed May 2025) and OpenPipe, Rubrik bought Predibase (Jun 2025), OpenAI bought neptune.ai (Dec 2025).

The new wave is RL/post-training as a service: Applied Compute went from $1.3B (Apr 2026) to reported talks at ~$3B (Aug 2026) on ~$12.8M ARR at the earlier round, showing investor enthusiasm well ahead of revenue.
RL environments are a new budget line: labs are reportedly weighing more than $1B of spend on them, and data-labeling firms are entering the space (Deeptune Series A context).

Inference leaders are moving down into training: Fireworks made its Training API GA (Aug 2026), and Modal plans RL/post-training products (Oct 2026). Standalone fine-tuning platforms are squeezed from both sides.

cats.title: Training data & RL environments
cats.overview: Labs buy expert human data and simulated “RL environments” to train their models. This became one of the largest revenue pools outside the labs, but it is a services business with labor-business margins.
happening: Mercor claims more than a $2B gross run-rate (mid-2026); its last closed round was at $10B, with $20B talks reported. Handshake runs at about $1B from AI training (April), and Snorkel at $375M.
These are gross figures. Contractors keep 60–70%, so net revenue is about a third of the headline.
After Meta bought 49% of Scale AI (June 2025), OpenAI left as a customer. Francis deSouza became Scale's CEO on Aug 10.
RL environments are the hot spot: Google paid more than $1.5B to license Mechanize's tech and hire its team (September), and AfterQuery repriced from $300M to $3.2B in about five months.
Legal risk is rising: Scale settled a contractor-misclassification suit for $12.5M, similar suits are pending against Mercor and Handshake, and Mercor had a data breach in March.

notes.note: Meta's ~$14.3B purchase of a 49% non-voting Scale AI stake (Jun 2025) led OpenAI to cut ties and Google/xAI to reportedly pause, Scale laid off ~14% of staff, and Scale now says its applications business will overtake data within 18 months - effectively vacating the top of the data market.

Human-data revenue is concentrated and huge: Mercor claims >$2B gross run-rate (Jun 2026), Handshake ~$1B AI-training run-rate (Apr 2026), micro1 claims $700M (Sep 2026), Snorkel >$375M (Sep 2026); YC's Garry Tan says more than a dozen YC data/RL-environment startups each top $10M/yr.
Headline figures are gross billings: contractors typically take 60-70%, so a $2B gross run-rate implies roughly $600-800M net and ~30% gross margins versus software-like margins elsewhere.

Spend is shifting to RL environments: Anthropic leaders reportedly discussed spending >$1B on RL environments in a year, and incumbents are buying in - Mercor acquired Sepal AI (Feb 2026) and Deeptune (Jul 2026), and Google paid $1.5B+ in a license-and-hire deal for Mechanize (Sep 2026) months after its $9.1M seed.

Labor and security liability is rising: Scale agreed to a $12.5M contractor-misclassification settlement, at least five more misclassification suits are pending in California (plus one in Texas) against firms including Mercor and Handshake, and Mercor's Mar 2026 LiteLLM breach triggered 7+ class actions and a Meta work pause.

Valuations for new entrants are extreme and crowded: Proximal raised a $15M seed at $300M and claims >$200M run-rate with ~40 people, AfterQuery repriced from $300M to $3.2B in ~5 months, and RL-List tracks 40+ environment/data vendors.

cats.title: Evals, observability & AI security
cats.overview: Tools that measure, monitor and secure AI systems. Large observability and security companies have been buying this layer quickly.
happening: Dynatrace bought Arize for $915M (agreed in August, completed by October), Cisco closed its Galileo purchase (May), ClickHouse bought Langfuse (January), and Humanloop's team joined Anthropic.
Most early AI-security startups were bought in 2025, by Palo Alto, SentinelOne, Check Point, CrowdStrike, F5 and Cato.
Braintrust is the main independent evals platform: $80M Series B at $800M (February).
2026 money moved to agent security and monitoring: Zenity $125M Series C, HiddenLayer $100M Series B, Gray Swan $40M Series A, and Goodfire (interpretability) $150M Series B at $1.25B.

notes.note: Incumbents are buying evals/observability startups: Dynatrace agreed to buy Arize for $915M (Aug 2026), Cisco/Splunk closed Galileo (May 2026), and ClickHouse bought Langfuse (Jan 2026).
Cisco completed its Galileo acquisition by May 22, 2026, folding agent evals and guardrails into Splunk Observability Cloud.
Dynatrace's CEO projected AI observability to exceed $10B by 2030 and pointed to fragmentation between eval tooling and app/infra monitoring.

Most early AI-security startups were absorbed in 2025: Palo Alto/Protect AI (closed Jul 2025), SentinelOne/Prompt Security (~$250M), Check Point/Lakera, CrowdStrike/Pangea (~$260M), F5/CalypsoAI, Cato/Aim.

Independent agent-security and agent-monitoring startups still raised large 2026 rounds (Zenity $125M C, HiddenLayer $100M B, Gray Swan $40M A, Raindrop A); the open space has moved from LLM-call evals to agent trajectories, simulation and runtime security.

cats.title: Databases for AI apps
cats.overview: AI apps need somewhere to keep data and embeddings. The big data platforms are winning: Postgres became the default database for agent-built apps, and pure vector databases are under pressure.
happening: Databricks raised $5B at $190B (August) on a run-rate above $7B growing 80%+. Its Postgres product, built on the Neon purchase, passed a $100M run-rate.
Supabase raised $500M at $10.5B (June) with about $170M ARR. ClickHouse raised $400M at a reported $15B (January) and runs at $250M.
More than 80% of Neon's databases were being created by AI agents as of May 2025.
Pinecone replaced its founder-CEO and reportedly explored a sale in 2025. Turbopuffer, much cheaper, reached about a $100M run-rate (Sacra estimate). Qdrant raised a $50M Series B (March).

notes.note: Databricks raised $5B at $190B in Aug 2026 on a $7B+ run-rate growing 80%+, and its Postgres product Lakebase (from the Neon deal) passed a $100M run-rate.
Platforms are grabbing Postgres: Databricks bought Neon, Snowflake bought Crunchy Data (~$250M, Jun 2025), and ClickHouse launched a managed Postgres service (Jan 2026).
Agents now create most new databases: over 80% of Neon databases were provisioned by AI agents (May 2025), and Supabase reported database count up 600% YoY at its $10.5B Series F (Jun 2026).

Standalone vector DBs face price compression: Pinecone lost Notion, replaced its founder-CEO and reportedly explored a sale (Sep 2025), while object-storage-based Turbopuffer, at roughly 10–30% of Pinecone's cost, reached an estimated ~$100M run-rate (Sacra, Mar 2026).
Some independent vector DBs can still raise: Qdrant closed a $50M Series B (Mar 2026), but most other pure-play vector DBs (Weaviate, Chroma, Zilliz) had no 2026 rounds that could be verified.

layers.intro: Software that builders use to make AI products: coding agents, app builders, review and testing, agent infrastructure, inference, training platforms, training data, evals and security, and databases.

layers.name: Applications
layers.what: Products people and businesses use: assistants, search, and vertical AI for legal, health, finance and more.

cats.title: Assistants, AI search & browsers
cats.overview: General-purpose assistants are where consumers meet AI. The labs' own apps (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) dominate. A few independents, led by Perplexity and Genspark, grew fast anyway, and most of the rest have been bought.
happening: Perplexity's ARR reportedly rose from under $250M at the start of 2026 to over $750M by August. Nvidia is reported to be in talks to invest at more than $30B, up from $20B in September 2025.
Genspark claims $250M+ ARR about a year after launch, and its valuation rose from $1.6B to $2.6B between March and June.
Most exits have been acquisitions: Atlassian bought The Browser Company for $610M, Meta bought Manus (reported $2B+), and Cognition bought Poke.
China's planning regulator ordered Meta to unwind the Manus deal in April, and Manus became independent again in August. It's a reminder that startups with roots in China carry geopolitical risk.
AI browsers are now a contest between incumbents: OpenAI's ChatGPT Atlas, Gemini in Chrome and Opera Neon.

notes.note: Perplexity's ARR reportedly went from under $250M at the start of 2026 to over $750M by August, with Nvidia discussing an equity stake at a valuation above $30B (up from $20B in Sep 2025).
General-agent apps scaled unusually fast: Genspark claims $250M+ ARR within about a year of launch and added ~$150M ARR in Q1 2026, raising its valuation from $1.6B (Mar) to $2.6B (Jun 2026).
Consolidation is the dominant exit: Atlassian bought The Browser Company for $610M (Sep 2025), Meta bought Manus for reportedly >$2B (Dec 2025) and Cognition bought Poke (Jul 2026).
Geopolitical risk is real for agent startups with China roots: China's NDRC ordered Meta to unwind its ~$2B Manus purchase in April 2026.

AI browsers are now an incumbent fight: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas (Oct 2025), Google integrated Gemini into Chrome, Opera charges $19.90/mo for Neon, and no independent body publishes AI-browser market share.

cats.title: Knowledge work & productivity
cats.overview: AI for the everyday work of office jobs: searching company knowledge, meeting notes, writing, email and slides. Demand is huge, but Google and Microsoft now bundle much of it into suites people already pay for.
happening: Glean went from $100M to $300M ARR in 15 months (May 2026), competing directly with Microsoft, Google and Amazon.
Granola raised $125M at $1.5B in March, a valuation about 6× higher than a year earlier, even though more than ten note-taking apps and devices compete.
Gamma reached $100M ARR profitably with about 50 people. Tome's founders dropped their 25M-user slides app to build a CRM (Lightfield).
Grammarly renamed itself Superhuman after buying Coda and the Superhuman email app, then bought GPTZero (June).
Google added Gemini, Meet note-taking and NotebookLM to standard Workspace plans, which undercuts standalone tools.

notes.note: Google raised Workspace prices and bundled Gemini, Meet note-taking and NotebookLM Plus into standard plans, ending $20-$30 AI add-ons and pressuring Microsoft's $30/user Copilot add-on - a direct threat to standalone notetakers and assistants.

AI notetaking is crowded: TechCrunch lists Granola, Zoom, Fireflies, Otter and Read AI on software plus Plaud, Mobvoi, Anker, Viaim and Vibe in hardware, with Plaud on track for $100M software revenue.
Despite crowding, investors still pay up for UX leaders: Granola's valuation rose ~6x to $1.5B in under a year with a $125M Series C.
Enterprise search has a scaled independent winner: Glean went from $100M to $300M ARR in 15 months, competing against Microsoft, Google and Amazon suites.
AI slides split into winner and casualty: Gamma reached $100M ARR profitably at a $2.1B valuation, while Tome's founders abandoned their 25M-user app to build the CRM Lightfield.

cats.title: Agent builders & workflow automation
cats.overview: No-code tools that let business users wire up AI agents and automations. It is the successor to RPA (software robots that click through screens) and to Zapier-style integrations, and big platforms are buying in.
happening: n8n's valuation went from about $350M (early 2025) to $2.5B (October 2025) to $5.2B through a share sale to SAP (May 2026). SAP is building n8n into its own agent tools.
OpenAI (AgentKit) and Google (Gemini Enterprise) launched their own visual agent builders.
Smaller players are being bought cheaply: Workday bought Sana, and Asana bought StackAI for $75M.
UiPath, the RPA leader, grew ARR only 11%, to $1.85B, while repositioning around agents.

notes.note: n8n's valuation went from about $350M (early 2025) to $2.5B (Oct 2025) to $5.2B via an SAP secondary in May 2026, with SAP embedding n8n in Joule Studio — the clearest sign enterprise suites will buy rather than build workflow-agent canvases.

Frontier labs entered directly: OpenAI launched AgentKit's visual Agent Builder at DevDay (Oct 2025), and Google rebranded Agentspace as Gemini Enterprise with a no-code agent workbench, squeezing standalone builders from above.
Consolidation is underway at small prices: Workday bought Sana (Nov 2025) and Asana bought YC-backed StackAI for $75M (May 2026), citing competition from Zapier and the AI labs.

RPA→agents shift is slow for incumbents: UiPath grew ARR only 11% to $1.853B in FY2026 while repositioning around 'agentic automation' (agreed WorkFusion acquisition, Screen Agent, Agentic AI Foundation membership), even as it reached first full-year GAAP profit.

Venture money still flows to business-user agent builders with traction: Gumloop raised a $50M Benchmark-led Series B (Mar 2026) and Dust a $40M Sequoia/Abstract Series B (May 2026), but the space is crowded with Zapier, Make, n8n, Lindy and the labs.

cats.title: Customer support & voice agents
cats.overview: Support is where companies first replaced human work with AI agents. They often pay per resolved ticket, and voice agents now take phone calls. It is one of the best-funded application categories and is consolidating fast.
happening: Sierra raised $950M at more than $15B (May) on about $150M ARR (February), roughly 100× revenue. Decagon is valued at $4.5B, Parloa at $3B and Wonderful at $2B.
Salesforce bought Fin, formerly Intercom, for about $3.6B (agreed in June, closed in September). Zendesk bought Forethought, and NICE bought Cognigy for $955M.
Pricing per resolution is falling: Fin charges $0.99, Zendesk $1.50–2.00, and HubSpot cut to $0.50 (April).
Voice infrastructure raised big: Deepgram at $1.3B and LiveKit at $1B (both January). LiveKit powers ChatGPT's voice mode.
A July comparison tracked eight funded phone-agent platforms, and a testing layer (Coval, Hamming, Roark) has formed on top of them.

notes.note: Outcome-based pricing is now the norm for packaged support agents: Fin charges $0.99 per resolution, Zendesk $1.50 (committed) to $2.00 per automated resolution, and HubSpot cut its Customer Agent from $1.00 per conversation to $0.50 per resolved conversation in April 2026, signaling per-resolution price compression; Salesforce Agentforce still prices per conversation/action.

Consolidation accelerated in 2026: Zendesk bought Forethought (March), Salesforce agreed to buy Fin (formerly Intercom) for about $3.6B (June) to complement Agentforce, which hit $1.2B ARR in Q1 FY27, and Sierra acquired Takeoff (July) after earlier buys of Opera Tech, Receptive AI and Fragment.

CCaaS incumbents are buying AI agents rather than partnering: NICE agreed to buy Cognigy for $955M (about 25x estimated $37M revenue, per Aragon Research), Five9 bought Inference, and SoundHound bought Amelia; analysts expect an M&A race as contact-center vendors shift from bring-your-own-agent to native AI.

Capital is concentrating in a few enterprise CX-agent leaders: Sierra raised $950M at $15B+ on $150M ARR (about 100x), versus Decagon at $4.5B (Jan 2026), Parloa at $3B (Jan 2026) and Wonderful at $2B (Mar 2026); Dealroom flags crowded competition and low switching costs as risks.

Voice-agent platforms are crowded: a July 2026 comparison tracks eight funded phone-agent startups (Vapi, Retell, Synthflow, Parloa, Bland, PolyAI, Replicant, Avoca), with 2026 rounds including Vapi $50M Series B, Bland $50M Series C, Avoca $125M Series B; infra layers raised too (Deepgram $130M at $1.3B, LiveKit $100M at $1B).

A voice-agent testing/eval sub-layer is forming and already has multiple funded players: Coval raised a $28M Series A (June 2026) and competes with Hamming and YC-backed Roark, which signals the voice stack is maturing past simple builders.

cats.title: Sales, marketing & GTM
cats.overview: AI for finding, contacting and winning customers. Data-driven prospecting tools like Clay won big. Fully autonomous “AI SDRs” (AI sales reps) hit a backlash. The new wave optimizes how brands show up in AI chatbot answers, called GEO or AEO.
happening: Clay raised $115M at $7.1B (September) and has 17,000+ customers.
GEO boom: Profound raised $180M at $1.8B (September), seven months after a $96M Series C. Platforms are already buying: Sitecore bought Scrunch and HubSpot bought XFunnel.

AI SDR backlash: in 2025, reports said 11x showed logos of companies that weren't customers. The FTC announced a proposed settlement with Air AI in March. Industry blogs (unaudited) cite 50–70% annual churn for AI SDR tools.
Salesforce's Agentforce passed about $1.2B ARR, and pricing is moving from seats to outcomes and usage (HubSpot, Gong, Clay).
Gong passed $500M ARR and is moving to token-based pricing.

notes.note: AI SDR backlash: TechCrunch reported in Mar 2025 that 11x displayed logos of non-customers and struggled with retention; its founder-CEO stepped down in May 2025.
Regulators are policing AI sales-agent hype: on Mar 24, 2026 the FTC announced a proposed settlement with Air AI, with an $18M judgment (mostly suspended) and a ban on selling business opportunities.
Industry blogs put annual AI SDR tool churn at 50-70% (attributed to UserGems), and funding has tilted toward 'augment the rep' tools like Letter AI and Hyperbound; treat churn figures as unaudited.
GEO funding wave: Dealroom counts seven GEO startups founded 2024-25 that raised $472M combined, with Profound taking ~71%; two (Scrunch, XFunnel) were already acquired.
Profound raised a $180M Series D at $1.8B in Sep 2026, under seven months after a $96M Series C, the steepest valuation ramp in GTM software this year.

Platforms are absorbing GEO: Sitecore bought Scrunch (~$225M per Bloomberg) in Jun 2026, HubSpot bought XFunnel, and Adobe and HubSpot ship built-in AEO features, squeezing standalone monitoring tools.
Salesforce's Agentforce reached ~$1.2B ARR (+205% YoY) in Q1 FY27, and Salesforce closed its Qualified acquisition (agentic inbound/AI SDR) on Apr 1, 2026.
Pricing shift to outcomes: from Apr 14, 2026 HubSpot charges $0.50 per resolved Customer Agent conversation and $1 per recommended lead, replacing per-conversation and per-contact fees.
Seat-based pricing is eroding: Gong plans token-volume pricing, and Clay split billing into data credits plus a per-action workflow meter in Mar 2026 (Sacra).
Per Crunchbase, sales, marketing and CRM startups raised ~$3.7B through early May 2026, on pace to match the ~$8B/yr of 2023-25 and far below 2021-22, with AI firms taking the majority.

cats.title: Finance & accounting
cats.overview: AI for corporate finance teams and accounting firms: closing the books, accounts payable and receivable, audit, and a new wave of AI-native accounting systems challenging NetSuite. Some investors are skipping software and buying accounting firms to run them with AI.
happening: Ramp raised $1.85B at $60B (Oct 15), up from $44B in June, and says annualized revenue passed $2B. Capital One closed its $5.15B purchase of Brex in April, below Brex's 2022 valuation of $12.3B.
Two AI accounting companies passed $1B valuations in 2026: Basis ($1.15B, agents for CPA firms) and Rillet ($1B, AI-native ERP with 600+ customers).
NetSuite challengers (Rillet, DualEntry, Campfire, Light, Everest, Doss) drew close to $0.5B of venture money in about a year.

Thrive Holdings, which owns the Crete CPA rollup, reportedly raised about $2B to buy accounting firms and rebuild them around AI. About half of the top 30 US CPA firms now have private-equity backing.

notes.note: AI-native ERP/GL challengers to NetSuite (Rillet, DualEntry, Campfire, Light, Everest, Doss) drew close to half a billion dollars of venture money in roughly a year — a crowded, well-funded race.
Two AI accounting companies crossed $1B valuations in 2026: Basis ($1.15B, Feb, selling agents to CPA firms) and Rillet ($1B, Aug, AI-native ERP with 600+ customers).

Accounting-firm roll-ups are the capital-heavy alternative to selling software: Thrive Holdings (owner of the Crete CPA roll-up) reportedly raised ~$2B from SoftBank, Altimeter and D1 to buy and AI-rewire services firms.
Almost half of the top 30 US CPA firms had private-equity investment or an alternative practice structure by early 2026, so AI vendors increasingly sell to PE-consolidated buyers.
Incumbents are consolidating spend platforms: Capital One closed its $5.15B Brex purchase (well below Brex's 2022 $12.3B valuation) while Ramp was reported raising at ~$60B pre-money.

cats.title: HR & recruiting
cats.overview: AI on both sides of hiring. Candidates mass-apply with AI, so employers buy AI sourcing, screening and interviewing to cope. The arms race drives demand, and it is also drawing legal attention.
happening: LinkedIn was handling about 11,000 applications per minute (+45% year over year), and Gartner projects about 1 in 4 applicants could be fake by 2028.
Juicebox raised $80M at $850M (March), Paraform a $40M Series B, and Metaview a $60M Series C (September).
Incumbents are buying: Workday closed its roughly $1B cash purchase of Paradox, and Salesforce absorbed Moonhub's team.
A January class action accuses Eightfold of violating US credit-reporting law (the FCRA) by scoring applicants without telling them. It is reportedly the first such suit against an AI hiring vendor.

notes.note: Volume arms race: LinkedIn was handling ~11,000 applications per minute (+45% YoY) as candidates mass-apply with AI, and Gartner projects ~1 in 4 applicants could be fraudulent by 2028 — driving demand for AI screeners.

Capital is concentrating in a few AI recruiting winners: HrFlow tallied $162.5M across seven March 2026 HR-tech deals, dominated by Juicebox ($80M) and Paraform, while PitchBook puts the median HR-tech VC round at only ~$2-3M.
The AI interviewer/screener wedge is crowded: TechCrunch lists Alex, HeyMilo, ConverzAI and Ribbon as direct competitors, and new voice-screening seeds (Ezra, Ringtime) kept arriving in 2026.
Incumbents are buying rather than building: Workday closed its ~$1B cash acquisition of Paradox (Oct 2025) to combine with HiredScore, and Salesforce absorbed Moonhub's team as it shut down.

Legal risk is rising for AI screening: a January 2026 proposed class action accuses Eightfold of violating the FCRA by scoring applicants without notice — reportedly the first such US suit against an AI hiring vendor.

cats.title: Security operations & IT
cats.overview: AI agents that work as security analysts and attackers: triaging alerts in the security operations center (SOC), running penetration tests, and handling IT tickets. Security buyers pay well, and incumbents are buying quickly.
happening: AI SOC is very crowded. KuppingerCole counted 123 vendors and expects only about 20 independent ones to survive to 2030.
Big recent rounds: 7AI $130M Series A, Exaforce $125M Series B at $725M, TENEX $250M Series B, Torq $140M Series D at $1.2B.
Autonomous pentesting is proving itself. HackerOne says AI “hackbots” filed 560+ valid reports, XBOW passed $1B, and Horizon3.ai went from $650M to more than $2B in about a year.
Buyers: Google closed its $32B Wiz purchase, Zscaler bought Red Canary, and Cribl bought CardinalOps and Radiant Security's tech.

notes.note: AI SOC is very crowded: KuppingerCole counted 123 AI SOC vendors (39 rated, 84 under screening) and expects only ~20 independent comprehensive vendors to survive to 2030.

Incumbents and data platforms are buying AI SOC tech: Zscaler closed Red Canary (Aug 2025) for agentic security ops, and Cribl bought Radiant Security's AI SOC assets (Aug 2026) after acquiring CardinalOps (Jul 2026); Google closed its $32B Wiz deal by March 2026.
Capital is concentrating in a few AI SOC leaders: 7AI raised a $130M Series A, Exaforce $125M Series B at $725M, TENEX $250M Series B and Torq $140M Series D at $1.2B within roughly six months.

Autonomous pentesting has measurable results: HackerOne's 2025 report says 'hackbots' submitted 560+ valid vulnerability reports with a 49% success rate, though complex bugs still need humans; XBOW says it reached #1 on the HackerOne leaderboard.

Offensive AI valuations are surging: Horizon3.ai went from $650M to >$2B in about a year (Series E, Aug 2026) and XBOW passed $1B (Series C, Mar 2026), while RunSybil, Terra and depthfirst raised fresh rounds in 2025-26.

cats.title: Legal
cats.overview: Legal is one of AI's clearest vertical wins. Lawyers bill for reading and writing, and models do both. Two well-funded leaders are racing, many Series A/B companies are still getting funded, and a new kind of AI-native law firm sells fixed fees instead of hours.
happening: Harvey raised $550M at $15.5B (September), up from $11B in March, at about $400M ARR (Sacra estimate). Legora reached $5.6B with over $200M ARR (estimate).
Crunchbase counts $4.6B into legal tech in 2025 (a record) and more than $2.2B in 2026 through August. 8 of the 12 largest 2026 rounds were Series A or B.
Consolidation: Legora made at least 5 acquisitions this year and Harvey at least 3. Clio bought vLex for $1B, and Wolters Kluwer bought Brightflag and Libra.
AI-native law firms are a new model: Crosby ($60M Series B), Norm Ai ($1.2B, which also runs a law firm) and Manifest OS ($60M Series A at $750M).

notes.note: Crunchbase counts $4.6B invested in legal/legal-tech startups in record 2025 and over $2.2B in 2026 through late August, mostly AI.
At least 12 legal tech rounds of $50M+ closed in 2026, 8 of the 12 largest were Series A or B, and 50+ seed rounds of $1M+ closed, so new entrants keep getting funded.
Valuation race: Harvey went from $11B (Mar 2026) to $15.5B (Sep 2026) while Legora tripled to about $5.6B with its Series D, and Harvey says 80% of the Am Law 100 use it.
Consolidation is underway: Legora made at least 5 and Harvey at least 3 acquisitions in 2026, and Wolters Kluwer bought Brightflag ($500M) and Libra ($105M).
Incumbents are buying in: Clio closed a $1B vLex acquisition (largest legal tech M&A to date) alongside a $500M Series G at $5B.

cats.title: Healthcare
cats.overview: Healthcare AI started with “ambient scribes” that write doctors' notes. Epic, the dominant medical-records vendor, now ships its own scribe, so the money is moving to clinical answers, patient-access agents, and billing and paperwork automation.
happening: Epic launched native AI Charting in February, and health systems began reconsidering separate scribe contracts. Independents keep raising anyway: Heidi $340M at $900M (September), Suki a $90M Series E (October).
OpenEvidence was valued at $12B in January and reached 1.12M verified US clinicians by September. A round at about $15B was reported but is unconfirmed.
Rock Health counted $7.4B of US digital-health funding in H1 2026, 115 acquisitions and zero IPOs.
Big 2026 rounds: Commure at $7B, Forus at $3B, Assort Health at $1.2B (patient phone agents), and Aidoc a $150M Series E.
Regulation is unsettled. The FDA's January guidance says nothing about generative AI, and the AMA published a framework for clinical AI agents in October.

notes.note: Epic launched native AI Charting (ambient scribe that drafts notes and queues orders) in Feb 2026, and health system leaders began reassessing separate contracts with Abridge, Ambience and Nabla.

Despite Epic's entry, independent scribes kept raising in fall 2026: Heidi took $340M at a $900M valuation with $50M ARR (Sep) and Suki raised a $90M Series E (Oct), both pivoting toward decision support and agentic workflows.

OpenEvidence hit a $12B valuation in Jan 2026 and 1.12M verified US clinician users by Sep 2026; Business Insider reported (via AI Weekly) a further round at ~$15B and founders fielding acquisition interest.
Rock Health counted $7.4B of US digital health VC across 244 deals in H1 2026, with 20 megadeals taking 45% of capital and no digital health IPOs so far in 2026.

Admin/RCM AI is consolidating: Rock Health tallied 115 digital health acquisitions in H1 2026, including R1 buying Humata Health and New Mountain combining SmarterDx and Thoughtful.ai into Smarter Technologies, while Abridge, Hippocratic AI and OpenAI (Torch) bought startups.

FDA's revised clinical decision support guidance (Jan 6, 2026) widened enforcement discretion for single-recommendation CDS but stayed silent on generative AI, leaving LLM clinical chatbots in regulatory gray area.

The AMA released a governance framework for agentic AI performing clinical functions in Oct 2026, saying clinical authority should be earned through evidence and will guide its work on liability and licensure.
Patient-access voice agents are crowded: Assort Health's $120M Series C at $1.2B (Jun 2026) came amid peers Artera, UnityAI, EliseAI, Hello Patient, Tennr and Prosper AI.

cats.title: Financial services & insurance
cats.overview: AI for banks, investors, insurers and financial advisors: research copilots, underwriting, lending decisions, and AI-native insurers that use models to price and serve customers. The labs are now selling finance products directly.
happening: AlphaSense raised $350M at $7.5B with more than $600M ARR. Rogo went from $750M to $2B between January and April and bought four companies.
Insurtech funding hit $2.44B in Q2 2026, the most since 2022, and 99.1% went to AI companies. Early-stage funding fell by half.
Corgi, an AI-native insurer for startups, raised twice in about three weeks: $1.3B, then $2.6B. It says it turned profitable in April.
Jump (AI for financial advisors) is used by about 1 in 10 US advisors. Anthropic launched Claude for Financial Advisors in September.

notes.note: Q2 2026 global insurtech funding hit $2.44B across 107 deals, the highest quarter since Q2 2022, with AI-focused firms taking 99.1%.
Insurtech capital is concentrating in late rounds: $100M+ deals totaled $1.67B in Q2 2026 while early-stage funding fell 51.8% QoQ to $264M.
AI finance-research valuations are re-rating fast: Rogo went from $750M (Jan 2026) to $2B (Apr 2026), and AlphaSense from $4B to $7.5B with $600M+ ARR.
AI wealth-advisor tooling is consolidating around two players: Jump ($105M raised, ~1 in 10 US advisors) has overtaken Zocks ($65M) in funding.

Frontier labs are entering finance directly: Zocks shipped integrations for Anthropic's new Claude for Financial Advisors (Sep 2026), and The Information framed Rogo/Hebbia growth against a 'Claude Finance threat'.

cats.title: Real estate & construction
cats.overview: AI for renting, buying, managing and building property: leasing agents, mortgage servicing, property-tax appeals, HOA management and construction progress tracking. It is a fragmented industry with old software, where a few AI leaders are scaling fast.
happening: EliseAI raised $350M at $4B (September), passed $200M ARR in June, and powers 1 in 6 US apartments.
Mortgage is heating up: Valon raised $150M at $2.3B (October) and says its agents work on 1 in 6 US mortgages. Vesta says AI-native lenders hold under 5% of originations.
Proptech funding was $4.53B in H1 2026, flat year over year, with a median round of $6.75M. Proptech leads all industries in $5–10M seed rounds.
HOA software leader Vantaca ($1.25B) bought the AI-native HOA startup HOAi. Ownwell raised a $50M Series B for property-tax appeals.

notes.note: Proptech venture funding was $4.53B across 231 rounds in H1 2026 (CRETI), roughly flat YoY (-0.6%), with a median round of $6.75M.
Proptech leads all industries in count of $5M-$10M seed rounds in 2026 (Crunchbase), signalling crowded early-stage AI tooling for agents, leasing and homeowners.
Vertical AI leaders are scaling fast in housing: EliseAI passed $200M ARR (Jun 2026) and powers one in six US apartments.
Mortgage is a hot AI battleground: Valon claims agents on 1 in 6 US mortgages and $200M+ contracted ARR, while origination challenger Vesta says AI-natives hold under 5% share vs incumbent ICE.
HOA software incumbents are absorbing AI-native startups: Vantaca (raised $300M+ at $1.25B) acquired YC startup HOAi and markets 'HOAi' agentic automation.

cats.title: Government & public sector
cats.overview: AI software for federal, defense and state and local government. Palantir is the giant, the labs sell to agencies at token prices, and a set of Series A/B companies is going after permits, procurement and defense analysis.
happening: Palantir's Q2 revenue was $1.935B (+93%), with US government up 90% and US commercial up 149%. It guides about $8.15B for 2026.
The labs' $1 federal deals are ending. OpenAI moved to usage pricing at a 50% discount on Oct 1, and Anthropic's $1 deal was extended only to Oct 31.
Govini reached $1.25B on more than $100M ARR. Defense-tech VC was $49.1B in 2025, mostly for hardware.
State and local AI is drawing Series A rounds: GovWell ($25M), FSH ($20M) and Polimorphic ($18.6M).

notes.note: Palantir's U.S. government revenue grew 90% YoY to $809M in Q2 2026 and it raised FY2026 revenue guidance to ~$8.15B, showing federal budgets shifting toward AI software at scale.
GSA's OneGov $1 pilots are ending: OpenAI moves federal ChatGPT to usage-based pricing at a 50% discount from Oct 1, 2026, after GSA said 3.5M federal employees used it in the pilot.
Anthropic's $1-per-user OneGov Claude deal was extended only to Oct 31, 2026, and GSA says it is renegotiating expiring OneGov offers with vendors, so frontier-lab federal pricing is in flux.
Defense-tech VC hit $49.1B in 2025 (+81% YoY per PitchBook), though most dollars went to hardware (Anduril, Saronic); software winners like Govini reached $1.25B on >$100M ARR.

State and local govtech AI is attracting multiple Series A rounds in 2025-2026 (GovWell $25M from Insight, FSH $20M from Lachy Groom, Polimorphic $18.6M from General Catalyst), with GovWell saying 80% of its deals displace legacy vendors.

cats.title: Education
cats.overview: AI tutors, language coaches and teacher tools. The labs give away study modes, Duolingo is adding AI conversation practice, and Chegg collapsed, so standalone startups have to win on outcomes or distribution through schools.
happening: Chegg's Q2 revenue fell 51% to $51.8M. Duolingo grew 18% to $298.5M and is rolling out AI video calls to most new paid subscribers.
OpenAI (ChatGPT Study Mode) and Anthropic (Claude Learning Mode) ship free study modes.
Teacher tools are crowded with free tiers: MagicSchool claims 7M+ educators and Brisk 1 in 3 US teachers.
Ed-tech venture money has favored later-stage deals in 2026. Gizmo's $22M Series A was one of the few early rounds.

notes.note: Chegg's Q2 2026 revenue fell 51% year over year to $51.8M, with Q3 guidance of $43-44M, as it repositions toward employability and skills.

Duolingo grew Q2 2026 revenue 18% to $298.5M with 58.7M DAUs (+23%) and is rolling AI Video Call conversation practice to most Super subscribers, overlapping AI-tutor startups like Speak and Praktika.

Frontier labs ship free study modes: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Study Mode for Free/Plus/Pro/Team users in July 2025, after Anthropic's Claude Learning Mode (April 2025), and Google offers Gemini Guided Learning.
Axios reported the ed-tech VC market has favored later-stage deals so far in 2026, making early consumer tutor rounds (e.g., Gizmo's $22M Series A) relatively scarce.
School-facing AI tools are crowded with free tiers: MagicSchool claims 7M+ educators and Brisk claims 1 in 3 US teachers, while Khanmigo teacher tools are free.

cats.title: Industrial, manufacturing & supply chain
cats.overview: AI-native factories, engineering simulation, chip-design agents, freight and procurement agents, and grid software. It is a reshoring and defense-industrial bet, and venture money has rushed in.
happening: Hadrian raised $1.37B at $7.87B (August), about 5× its valuation a year earlier. US manufacturing VC roughly doubled to about $50B in 2025 (aggregator citing J.P. Morgan).
AI chip design is crowding fast: Ricursive ($300M Series A), ChipAgents ($74M) and Cognichip ($60M), all against Synopsys and Cadence.
PhysicsX (AI engineering simulation) raised $300M at about $2.4B in June.
Freight-broker agents are crowded: Augment, HappyRobot, Cargofy and Nexcade. Grid AI is drawing Series A money because of data-center power demand.
Factory startups also fail: Daedalus entered insolvency in October.

notes.note: Hadrian raised $1.37B at $7.87B in Aug 2026, about 5x its $1.6B valuation 13 months earlier, setting a high bar for AI-native factory startups.

U.S. manufacturing VC roughly doubled from ~$25B (2024) to ~$50B (2025) with ~$22B in Q1 2026 alone, per J.P. Morgan data cited by an aggregator; yet failures appear too (factory startup Daedalus entered insolvency in Oct 2026).
AI chip-design is crowding fast: Ricursive ($300M Series A, Jan 2026), ChipAgents ($74M, Feb 2026) and Cognichip ($60M, Apr 2026) all raised against incumbents Synopsys and Cadence.

Freight/logistics AI agents are a crowded category: Augment ($85M A), HappyRobot ($44M B at ~$500M, now announcing a C), Cargofy ($11M A, Jun 2026) and Nexcade ($6M seed, Jul 2026) all sell email/voice agents to brokers and forwarders.
AI-for-engineering simulation re-rated: PhysicsX raised $300M at ~$2.4B in June 2026 (from ~$1B), in what Bloomberg calls a crowded field that includes a Bezos-backed rival.
Grid/utility AI is drawing Series A capital driven by data-center power demand: GridCARE $64M (May 2026), Buzz Solutions $20M (Aug 2026), GridSight $36M (Sep 2026).

cats.title: Consumer apps & companions
cats.overview: AI products sold directly to people: companions, personal agents, voice dictation, shopping, health and devices. The labs' own apps dominate spending, a few new apps broke out, and the companion category ran into lawsuits, regulation and bankruptcy.
happening: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 on Oct 12. Compute costs of $56.1M (January–August) dwarfed revenue that peaked at about $5.3M a month. Disney made a $20M opening bid for an IP license and offered jobs to most of the staff.
a16z's October top-100 found that 4.5% of US consumers pay for ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude. Only 11 newcomers made the list, the fewest ever.
Breakouts: Instinct, a personal agent over text message, raised $1B at $10B, about a month after reports of a round at $2.5B. Wispr (voice dictation) reached $2B, and Whoop $10.1B.

Regulation: California's companion-chatbot law (SB 243) took effect in January, and the FTC opened an inquiry. Meta sold 7M+ smart glasses in 2025, while Humane shut down its pin and agreed to sell its assets to HP.

notes.note: Consumer AI spend is highly concentrated: 4.5% of US consumers paid for ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude in Aug 2026 (vs 2.1% a year earlier); the top 1% of spenders made 19.5% of spend and only 13% of payers pay for a second AI product.

Lab apps dominate: ChatGPT has ~2x Gemini's and ~6x Claude's web visits and ~3x their US paid subscribers; only 11 newcomers entered a16z's 7th-edition top 100, the fewest ever, and incumbents (Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots) launched personal agents in Sep 2026.

Companion regulation tightened: California SB 243 (signed 2025-10-13, effective 2026-01-01) mandates AI disclosure, break reminders and self-harm protocols with a private right of action, and the FTC opened a 6(b) inquiry into seven chatbot companies in Sep 2025.
Character.AI filed Chapter 11 on 2026-10-12 after compute costs ($56.1M Jan-Aug 2026) dwarfed revenue (peak ~$5.3M/month) amid teen-harm suits; Disney bid $20M for an IP license and hired most staff.
AI devices split: Meta sold 7M+ smart glasses in 2025 (about 3x 2024), while Humane shut down its AI Pin and agreed to sell its assets to HP for $116M (Feb 2025).

layers.intro: Products that businesses and people use, first by business function (support, sales, finance, HR, security) and then by industry (legal, healthcare, financial services, real estate, government, education, industrial and consumer).

layers.name: Physical AI & robotics
layers.what: Models that act in the physical world: humanoids, robot foundation models, autonomy.

cats.title: Robot foundation models & data
cats.overview: Labs are trying to build one “robot brain” that works across many bodies, the way LLMs work across many tasks. The bottleneck is data, since robots lack an internet's worth of examples, so robot-data companies have become a business of their own.
happening: Skild AI raised about $1.4B at more than $14B (January) on about $30M of 2025 revenue. Physical Intelligence was reported in talks at more than $11B, double its last confirmed $5.6B.
Generalist went from $2B to about $3B between June and August, and Genesis AI was in talks at $3B.
Robot data is booming: XDOF approached a $50M run-rate, and Mecka AI raised $60M from Sequoia. The largest open dataset has only about 3,000 hours.
Nvidia (GR00T, Cosmos) and Google DeepMind (Gemini Robotics) give away base models, which pressures the labs.

notes.note: Robot-brain valuations re-rated sharply: Skild AI raised ~$1.4B at >$14B in Jan 2026 (3x in ~7 months), and Physical Intelligence was reported in talks at >$11B, double its $5.6B mark.
Second-tier model labs are scaling fast too: Generalist went from $2B (June) to ~$3B (August 2026) and Genesis AI was in talks at $3B pre-money, so the top tier now has at least four $3B+ players.

Robot data is the bottleneck and a new business: XDOF approached ~$50M annualized revenue and sought a ~$1.2B valuation, Mecka AI raised $60M from Sequoia, while Scale AI and micro1 are expanding into robot data.
Open datasets are tiny by LLM standards: Config says its 100,000+ hours of human motion data is 30x the ~3,000 hours in AgiBot World, the largest comparable open-source set.

Big tech is commoditizing the base layer: NVIDIA ships open GR00T N1.6, Cosmos world models and Isaac Lab-Arena on Hugging Face, and Google DeepMind put Gemini Robotics models into Boston Dynamics' Atlas and Apptronik's Apollo.

cats.title: Humanoids
cats.overview: Human-shaped robots meant to work in factories, warehouses and eventually homes. China leads in units shipped. US companies lead in valuation and are now protected by an import ban, but real deployments are still small.
happening: About 13,000 humanoids shipped worldwide in 2025 and about 22,000 in H1 2026. The top five makers, all Chinese, held 86%.
In July the FCC banned imports of new foreign-made humanoids and robot dogs, walling off the US market.
Unitree raised about $904M in an August Shanghai IPO and soared, then fell more than 40%. Agility is going public through a $2.5B SPAC, with the shareholder vote set for Nov 2.
US valuations: Figure $39B (September 2025), Apptronik more than $5.5B, Sunday Robotics $1.15B. Mobileye bought Mentee for $900M.

notes.note: Global humanoid shipments were ~13,000 units in 2025 (Omdia), led by China's AgiBot (5,168), Unitree (4,200) and UBTech (1,000).
In H1 2026 global humanoid shipments reached ~22,000 units (Counterpoint); the top five makers (AgiBot, Unitree, Galbot, UBTech, Leju) are all Chinese and held 86% of shipments.
The FCC banned imports of new foreign-made humanoids and robot dogs on national-security grounds in July 2026, effectively walling the US market off from Chinese volume leaders.

Public markets opened then cooled: Unitree raised ~$904M in an August 2026 Shanghai IPO and soared on debut, then fell >40% while Chinese regulators reportedly tightened humanoid IPO approvals; Agility is pursuing a $2.5B US SPAC merger.
China-based robotics startups raised $5.6B across 176 deals in 2026 through mid-May, already above all of 2025 ($4.3B); China accounts for over 43% of global robotics venture investment.

cats.title: Industrial, warehouse & field robots
cats.overview: Robots that already earn money: warehouse automation, construction equipment, agriculture and inspection. AI makes them more flexible, and mega Series A rounds have arrived.
happening: Robotics venture funding hit $18.8B by June 2026, already above all of 2025 ($15B).
Mega Series A rounds: Mind Robotics (a Rivian spinout) $500M at $2B, Rhoda AI $450M, Theker $85M. Bedrock Robotics raised a $270M Series B for autonomous construction.
Symbotic, the scaled public player, earned $721M in its fiscal Q3 with a $22.5B backlog. It bought Fox Robotics.
Amazon halted its Blue Jay sorting robot after under six months, a sign that even giants struggle with manipulation.

notes.note: Robotics venture funding hit $18.8B globally by June 2026, already above full-year 2025 ($15B) and the 2021 peak ($14.1B).

Mega Series A rounds are now common in industrial AI robotics: Mind Robotics ($500M at $2B) and Rhoda AI ($450M at $1.7B) in one March 2026 week; Theker's $85M was called Europe's largest robotics Series A.
Consolidation is under way: Symbotic bought Fox Robotics (Feb 2026), Skild AI bought Zebra's robotics unit (Apr 2026), and Amazon bought Rivr and Fauna (Mar 2026).
Amazon passed 1 million warehouse robots in July 2025, but halted its Blue Jay sorting robot in Feb 2026 after under six months, showing in-house incumbents also struggle with manipulation.
Symbotic, the scaled public warehouse-automation player, reported $721M fiscal Q3 2026 revenue (+22% YoY), a $55M profit, and a $22.5B backlog.

cats.title: Autonomous vehicles & trucking
cats.overview: Self-driving cars finally work at scale, but one company, Waymo, is far ahead. Others are partnering with Uber to catch up, and driverless trucking is still at pilot scale.
happening: Waymo raised $16B at $126B (February). By Sept 1 it gave 500K+ paid rides a week with 4,000+ vehicles in 14 cities, and it targets 1M a week by year-end.
AV startups raised a record $21.4B through mid-April across just 34 deals, about three-quarters of it Waymo's round.
Tesla runs mixed supervised and unsupervised robotaxis in six metros, and Zoox charges for rides only in Las Vegas. Uber has deals for Waabi, Nuro/Lucid and Wayve fleets.
Trucking: Aurora guided only $14–16M of 2026 revenue while aiming for 200 driverless trucks.

notes.note: AV startups raised a record $21.4B across just 34 deals through Apr 15, 2026 (vs $5.9B across 99 deals in all of 2025); Waymo's $16B round was about three-quarters of it, so capital is highly concentrated in a few players.
Waymo reported 500K+ paid rides per week, 4,000+ vehicles and 14 US cities as of Sept 1, 2026, targeting 1M weekly trips by end of 2026 (up from 400K+/week across 6 metros in Feb).

US challengers lag well behind Waymo: Tesla runs mixed supervised/unsupervised robotaxis in six TX/FL metros, Zoox began paid rides only in Las Vegas (Aug 2026), and Motional, Avride and May Mobility still run with safety operators.
Uber has become the aggregator of non-Waymo stacks, with milestone-linked deals for 25,000 Waabi robotaxis, a 35,000-vehicle Nuro/Lucid program and Wayve fleets in 10 cities.
Driverless trucking is still pre-scale: Aurora guided 2026 revenue of only $14-16M while aiming for 200 driverless trucks by year-end, and Kodiak (public via SPAC, Sept 2025) runs a few dozen trucks.

cats.title: Defense tech & drones
cats.overview: Venture-backed defense companies building autonomous drones, boats, missiles and weapons systems, funded by record venture money and new Pentagon buying programs. Europe has its own surge.
happening: Defense startups raised $14.6B+ by about May 2026, more than all of 2025. Dealroom counts $17.4B by early July.
Mega-rounds: Anduril $5B at $61B (2025 revenue above $2B), Helsing $1.8B at $18B (Europe's largest round), Castelion $1B at $13B, Shield AI at $12.7B, Saronic at $9.25B.
The Pentagon's Drone Dominance program plans $1B+ for about 340,000 small attack drones, pushing unit prices toward about $2,300.
Pentagon spending on top defense startups has tripled since 2022 but is still under 1% of contracts (WSJ, via an aggregator).

notes.note: Defense-related startups raised more than $14.6B in roughly the first five months of 2026 across 107 rounds, already surpassing 2025's $9.6B record; Crunchbase flags nearly four dozen as likely IPO candidates.

Dealroom counts a record $17.4B raised by defense-tech startups by early July 2026, vs $11.2B in all of 2025, with mega-rounds dominating (Anduril $5B, Shield AI ~$2B, Saronic $1.75B, Helsing $1.8B, Quantum Systems $1.2B).

The Pentagon's Drone Dominance Program plans $1B+ over two years and four phases to buy ~340,000 small one-way attack drones, pushing unit prices from ~$5,000 toward ~$2,300; 25 vendors entered Phase I in Feb 2026.

European defense startups are surging: Helsing's $1.8B round at $18B was Europe's largest ever, alongside Quantum Systems ($1.2B), Stark (EUR 500M), Kraken ($175M Series B) and Harmattan AI ($200M Series B) in H1 2026.

Primes are co-investing: Lockheed Martin Ventures grew its fund from $400M to $1B in April 2026; meanwhile WSJ reports Pentagon spending on top defense-tech startups tripled since 2022 but remains under 1% of contracts (via aggregator).

layers.intro: AI that acts in the physical world: robot foundation models, humanoids, industrial robots, self-driving vehicles, and defense autonomy.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.leaders: Sam Altman (CEO); Greg Brockman (President, took over the product org in Apr 2026); Sarah Friar (CFO); Jakub Pachocki (Chief Scientist); Mark Chen (Chief Research Officer); Bret Taylor (Chair); Fidji Simo stepped down as CEO of Applications in Jul 2026, with no permanent successor named in the sources checked.

companies.flagship: GPT-6 family: GPT-6 Astra (top tier, GA Sep 4 2026), GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna (Sep 22 2026), GPT-6.1 Sol (about Sep 30 2026, near-Astra on agentic coding at roughly 1/5 the cost). GPT-6 rolled out to all ChatGPT users Oct 7 2026. Products: ChatGPT (including ChatGPT Work) and Codex.

recent: 2026-10: Acquired Orchestra Bio (AI agents for biotech operations) for its life-sciences work; terms undisclosed.
2026-06: Filed confidentially with the SEC for an IPO, the third major AI developer to do so.
2026-07: Fidji Simo left the Applications CEO role. At least 14 senior executives departed in 2026, including COO Lightcap and CRO Dresser.
